junction.name: Florida Avenue Northwest & 7th Street Northwest, Washington DC

claims.text: Florida Avenue Northwest & 7th Street Northwest had 95 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 23 pedestrians injured, 15 cyclists injured and 0 people killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $6.5 million a year.
5% of crashes here had a pedestrian hurt, against 3% at the city's worst crash locations.
4% of crashes here had a cyclist hurt, against 2% at the city's worst crash locations.

This corner got Leading Pedestrian Interval signals in 2019. Across the city: at 267 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-19%, 95% interval -35% to +1%) could be zero. Repeating it here is not supported by the city's own record.
The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: not shown (at 267 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-19%, 95% interval -35% to +1%) could be zero).

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 2.9 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $976,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.

Yellow Change Intervals would avoid about 1.5 crashes a year (CMF 4219, the more conservative of the two middle records of 4; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $507,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red; the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice.
The District Department of Transportation (DDOT) is responsible for 7th Street Northwest, Bohrer Street Northwest (no route reference, so presumed a city street).

The state transportation department (route designation only; confirm ownership) is responsible for Florida Avenue Northwest, Georgia Avenue Northwest (signed route in OpenStreetMap; owner not confirmed).
A request letter to the District Department of Transportation (DDOT) and the state transportation department (route designation only; confirm ownership) is ready to draft from these facts.
